transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… it’s mostly driving over those long bridges toward Miami. As soon as my car gets onto one, my chest tightens and I grip the wheel, and I just feel like I have to get off right away… even though I can’t.
Does this feeling of anxiety happen only when you're driving over bridges?

Mostly, yes. It’s really when my car gets onto those long bridges toward Miami… almost right away my chest tightens, my hands clamp onto the wheel, and I get this feeling like I have to get off, even though there’s nowhere to go.
Do you experience this kind of anxiety in any other situations where you might feel trapped or unable to escape?
I don’t think so… not that I’ve really noticed. It’s mainly the bridges.
Do you often worry about things in general, even when you're not driving over bridges?
No… I wouldn’t say that. I mean, I worry about normal things, I suppose, but not all the time. It’s really that bridge situation that gets to me.
Do you feel anxious when you think about driving over bridges when you are not actually on a bridge?

Yes… sometimes. I know those bridges are safe, and people cross them all day. But if I start thinking about driving over all that open water, it feels… bigger than it should. The fear gets ahead of me.
Do you typically worry about other specific things or situations besides driving over bridges?
Not really… nothing comes to mind. It’s mostly just the bridges.
Do you feel anxious when you are in other high places, like tall buildings or mountains?
I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve noticed that much. It’s not really something I can say for certain.
Do you feel anxious in enclosed spaces, like elevators or small rooms?
I don’t think so… elevators don’t really bother me much. Small rooms, not that I’ve noticed.
Do you think you could overcome your anxiety and drive over a bridge if you really had to?

If I really had to… maybe, but I’ve been avoiding it more than I’d like to admit. I’ve turned down things—gallery openings, birdwatching trips, even seeing my daughter sometimes—unless someone else can do the driving over the bridges. It’s embarrassing. I used to handle all of that myself.
Do you feel anxious most of the time, even when you're not thinking about bridges?
I don’t think so… not most of the time. I suppose I have my moments, but I haven’t really noticed it unless something brings it up.
Do you often find yourself worrying about potential problems or dangers even when there's no obvious reason to do so?
Not really, no. I don’t think I sit around worrying about things for no reason… at least, I haven’t noticed that.
Do you feel like your anxiety about bridges is affecting other parts of your life besides just driving over them?

Yes… I suppose it is. I’ve missed some of my senior-center exhibition meetings, and I have to depend on other people for trips down to Miami. It makes me feel… less independent, I guess. Less involved with the things and family responsibilities that used to keep my week in order.
Do you feel anxious in situations where you are not in control, outside of driving over bridges?
I’m not sure… I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed that, outside of the bridge situation.
Do you feel anxious when you are in situations that have nothing to do with bridges or heights?
No… I don’t think so. Not that I can recall. It’s mostly just those situations with bridges, as far as I’ve noticed.
Do you feel like you worry about a wide range of things, not just bridges?
No… I don’t think I’d say a wide range. I mean, I worry about ordinary things, I suppose, but not in the same way. It’s really more about the bridges.
Do you think your anxiety would improve if you were able to completely avoid driving over bridges?

Yes… I think it would. I’ve already started avoiding things, really—gallery openings, birdwatching trips, even some visits with my daughter—unless someone else can do the driving over the bridges. It’s embarrassing to admit. I’ve always been the one who handled plans myself.
Is your anxiety about bridges something that you think about and worry about even when you're not actually planning to drive over one?

Yes… sometimes. Not all the time, but if it comes to mind, I can feel it. I know those bridges have been there forever and people cross them every day, but when I picture driving over all that open water… it just feels much more dangerous than I know it really is.
Are there any other specific situations, besides driving over bridges, that trigger anxiety for you?
Not that I can think of, no. It’s really… the bridges that stand out.
Do you feel like your anxiety is mostly about bridges or is it starting to affect how you feel about other things in your life as well?

Mostly the bridges, I think. I mean… I know they’ve been there for years, and people go over them every day. But when I imagine driving over all that water, it feels much more frightening than it ought to.
Do you feel anxious about a variety of everyday things, not just bridges?

No… not really a variety of things. It’s mostly the bridges. I know they’re safe enough, people cross them all the time, but when I think about being over all that water, the fear just feels… bigger than it should.
